subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add a scoped `models status --probe --all` configured-model health sweep now, fold this behavior into broader fallback or migration diagnostics, or defer it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent CLI contract affects live provider calls, auth/profile routing, JSON output, fallback diagnostics, and overlap with other open model-safety requests.

options.title: Approve Scoped Status Probe
options.body: Add `--probe --all` as an opt-in status mode that preserves the current default probe behavior while sweeping configured model candidates with documented cost, timeout, filtering, and JSON semantics.

options.title: Fold Into Model Safety UX
options.body: Make the all-model sweep part of a broader fallback-chain or staged-migration design so users see one coherent model-safety workflow instead of several partial commands.

options.title: Defer The New Mode
options.body: Keep current provider/auth probes and model scan behavior unchanged until maintainers want to own the live per-model probing contract.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped Status Probe
recommendation.body: Add `--probe --all` as an opt-in status mode that preserves the current default probe behavior while sweeping configured model candidates with documented cost, timeout, filtering, and JSON semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current probe behavior and has the strongest history across model status, provider auth, and fallback-sensitive review decisions.
